title: Droshak
description: The official newspaper and organ of the Armenian Revolutionary Federation (ARF). The excerpt notes an issue from November 15, 1895, providing historical news on revolutionary activities in Shatakh.

title: Inhale and Exhale
description: A book by American-Armenian author William Saroyan. It contains reflections on the Armenian Revolutionary Federation and its struggle for the Armenian cause.

title: General Andranik Speaks
description: An extensive article originally published in the Paris newspaper 'Apaga' in 1924, later reprinted in 'Sovetakan Hayastan'. It explains the historical context behind Andranik's departure from the Dashnaktsutyun party.

title: Arpi
description: A magazine that was published for a long time by Hovsep Tadeosyan. It featured sections for children and teenagers.

title: It Was the Testament of the Martyrs
description: A book written by Karo Sasuni that tells the true story of Arshavir Shirakian. The author describes it as an extraordinary and authentic biography.

title: The A. R. F. Has Nothing Left to Do
description: A booklet written by Hovhannes Katchaznouni published in Vienna. It discusses the ideological state of the party following the disasters of the First Republic.

title: Memoirs
description: A collection of personal recollections by Bishop Yeghishe Chilingirian. It was published separately in 1920 in Alexandria.

title: Hayastan
description: A newspaper founded by Tigran Khachikian with the support of the Balkan Central Committee. It aimed to expose the atrocities and massacres committed by the Ittihad regime to the civilized world.

title: Mir-Hazo
description: The first novel by Malkhas (Artashes Hovsepyan) published in 1902. It reflects the author's early literary work within the revolutionary movement.

title: Revolutionary Short Stories
description: A collection of four stories published as a small book. It captures the spirit of the revolutionary struggle through narrative fiction.

title: Sadayelakan
description: A three-act drama by Ghevond Meloyan published in Paris in 1965. It represents one of the final works by this veteran revolutionary and writer.

title: The Evening of Farewell
description: A notable work by Levon Shant that was serialized in the newspaper Hairenik. It emerged during the realistic period of Western Armenian literature in the late 19th century.

title: Paths of Life
description: This is a memoir authored by Simon Vratsian. It provides personal insights into his experiences and his political journey within the Armenian Revolutionary Federation.

title: My Soul in My Hands
description: This is a memoir written by Arshavir Shirakian detailing his experiences as an Armenian fedayi and participant in the Nemesis operation. The text reflects on the intense personal history of the author.

title: Memoirs of the Kukunian Expedition
description: These memoirs detail the experiences of Hovsep Movsisian during the Kukunian expedition. The text was published in Hairenik magazine between December 1933 and April 1935.

title: Andranik's Funeral
description: An article published in the Hairenik newspaper regarding the historical perception and legacy of the Armenian military leader Andranik Ozanian.

title: The Village
description: A literary work mentioned as authored by the writer. It signifies the author's contribution to Armenian literature.

title: Hairenik
description: A monthly journal that publishes analytical articles and studies regarding the ARF program. It acts as a forum for ideological debate and historical documentation.

title: The Expedition of the Kukunian Group
description: This is a historical booklet published by the A.R.F. press in 1894. It chronicles the revolutionary expedition led by student Sargis Kukunian from the Caucasus into Western Armenia.

title: Khanasor Expedition
description: This is a significant event in the history of the Armenian revolutionary struggle. It details the retaliatory march of Armenian fedayi forces against the Mazrik tribe in 1897.

title: Hairenik Monthly
description: A cultural publication founded by Ruben Darbinian. It is dedicated to Armenian literature, history, and the history of the Armenian revolutionary movement.

title: How I Became a Dashnak
description: An article/memoir written by Simon Vratsian in 1947. It reflects on the accidental and inevitable turns in life that lead individuals toward political commitment.

title: Bolshevism and the Dashnaktsutyun
description: A valuable work published in 1949 by Vahan Navasardian. It contains a specific chapter titled 'Why We Fight' that serves as the author's political testament.

title: Andranik's Memoirs
description: A collection of memories and historical accounts documenting the activities in Sasun and Mush. It features details on revolutionary solidarity and key figures such as Serob and various local leaders.
